findings.comment: renderer->defragInProgress is set to 1 at the beginning of VULKAN_INTERNAL_DefragmentMemory, but it is never reset back to 0 on any return path (neither on allocation failure nor on successful completion). Because VULKAN_Submit checks '!renderer->defragInProgress' before calling defragmentation, defragmentation will run at most once during the renderer's entire lifetime and will permanently block subsequent defragmentations.

In VULKAN_INTERNAL_CycleActiveTexture, VULKAN_INTERNAL_TextureTransitionToDefaultUsage is called with texture before checking if texture is NULL. If VULKAN_INTERNAL_CreateTexture fails (for example due to out-of-memory), texture will be NULL, causing a null pointer dereference inside VULKAN_INTERNAL_TextureTransitionToDefaultUsage.
The error message says 'Failed to allocate defrag buffer!' in the texture creation failure path.
